notes: Temple is wide rooms joined by narrow halls, with the pickups concentrated high and a single armour. That combination makes it the most vertical arena and the one where holding the top floor is closest to holding the map.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: There is exactly one body armour, so it is a single contested point rather than a circuit; whoever holds it holds a standing advantage until it is taken from them.
nuance.because: Temple carries a single Armour record, matching Basement and against three in Complex and Library.

nuance.claim: The armour and the better weapons sit at or near the top of the structure, so the upper floor is worth holding for supply reasons before any positional ones.
A large opening in the upper floor looks down into the room below, which is a free firing position on anyone crossing it who has not thought to look up.
The wide rooms give the long sightlines that most arenas lack, so long-range weapons are genuinely strong here rather than merely usable.
The open rooms give explosives room to travel without catching the firer, which is not true of the tighter arenas.
Several doors are concealed in the walls, so a player can leave a room by a route an opponent does not know exists and reappear from an unexpected side.
Because the wide rooms connect only through a small number of doorways, mining the doors covers nearly all movement on the map.
nuance.because: Temple carries six Door records against forty-one pads, so the doorways are a genuinely small set relative to the space.

nuance.claim: The corridors joining the rooms are tight enough that an explosive fired inside one kills the firer as readily as the target.
The rooms are large enough that a moving target at range is hard to hit, so an outgunned player is better off in the open here than in a corridor.
With only five spawn points, spawn denial is a viable strategy here rather than an opportunistic bonus.
nuance.because: Temple carries five Spawn records, the joint fewest of any arena.

nuance.claim: In split-screen play the concealed doors give away nothing to the opponent who is watching your pane, so on this map screen-watching decides where ambushes land.
The open rooms make it forgiving for weaker players, since distance and space substitute for reaction time in a way the corridor maps do not allow.
One-hit kills plus long sightlines make the upper floor overwhelming, so control of the top is close to a win condition in this mode.
An unarmed carrier should stay in the narrow connecting halls rather than the rooms, because the open space that protects an armed player exposes a defenceless one.
Against the map's stone colouring, uniformed characters in muted tones are harder to pick out across the large rooms than brightly dressed ones.
The loop of rooms and halls sustains long chases, so a damaged player can usually break away rather than being cornered, which makes finishing kills harder than on other maps.
